title: Over 500 escalators across four MRT lines to be refurbished, Singapore News

 singapore Over 500 escalators across four MRT lines to be refurbished
 From Dec 17, 290 escalators across four MRT lines will be progressively upgraded, while another 237 on the Circle Line will be refurbished later. More than 500 escalators across the MRT's North-South, East West, North-East and Circle Lines are set to be progressively upgraded to ensure their safety, reliability and commuter comfort. PHOTO: AsiaOne/Danial Zahrin PUBLISHED ON November 19, 2026 11:01 AM BY Sean Ler More than 500 escalators across the MRT's North-South, East-West, North-East and Circle lines are set to be progressively refurbished from Dec 17.
 The Land Transport Authority (LTA) announced this in a joint news release with public transport operators SBS Transit and SMRT on Thursday (Nov 19).
 Works will progressively begin on some 290 escalators across the North-South and East-West Lines (NSEWL), and North East Line (NEL) from Dec 17, and are expected to be completed by 2032.
 A further 237 escalators on the Circle Line will also be refurbished but at a later date to be announced.
 LTA said the refurbishment programme is part of ongoing efforts to ensure that the escalators continue to operate safely and reliably for commuters.
 What rail commuters can look forward to
 According to LTA, the refurbished escalators will feature enhanced safety and operational features such as in-built voice announcement system for safety announcements, LED indicators to indicate the direction of travel, and improved illumination.
 It added that the escalators will be able to operate at dual speeds — regular and slower. 
 This allows escalators to operate at regular speed during peak hours to facilitate smooth commuter flow, and at a slower speed during off-peak hours for energy conservation purposes and to better serve the ageing population.
 The upcoming round of refurbishment includes 83 escalators along the NSEWL, which LTA said was not covered in its earlier upgrading of 231 escalators on the two lines in 2022, as they were not yet due then.
 Each escalator will take about four to five months to refurbish as works involve the replacement and upgrading of key mechanical and electrical components, including the motor, control equipment, steps, handrails and safety features.
 At stations where more than one escalator is scheduled for refurbishment, works will be sequenced to minimise inconvenience to commuters.
 LTA and the two public transport operators reassured commuters that at least one up-riding escalator will remain in service to carry passengers from the platforms to concourses, and to the entrances.
 Lifts will also remain available for commuters who require them.
 The refurbishment programme will also include escalators adjacent to stations, such as at pedestrian overhead bridges.
 Ridership on NSEWL and NEL 
 Checks by AsiaOne show that while an escalator's refurbishment is usually linked with its design life as recommended by the manufacturer, typically at around 25 to 35 years based on industrial practice.   
 However, the actual useful life of an escalator is ultimately determined by its operating condition, which is affected by the runtime, workload, maintenance quality and vibration, in addition to age.
 The NSEWL are Singapore's oldest MRT lines and began operations in the 1980s, while the NEL — the world's first fully automated driverless heavy rail rapid transit line — opened in 2003.
 MRT ridership climbed 2.29 per cent to 3.49 million daily trips in 2025.
 Data from LTA shows that NSEWL stations and NEL stations rank about the top 25 busiest stations in Singapore.
